foreground planes. Establish a strong static composition before adding motion.

Opaque continuations require deliberate crop/mask blending.

title: Clothes Rack Showroom
description: A 3D clothing showroom with two racks, a responsive camera and interactive product browsing.
prompt:
# Clothes Rack Showroom — complete working prompt

Create an immersive, responsive clothing showroom with a real-time Three.js room, two clothing rails on perpendicular walls, scroll-controlled entry, a camera that responds to desktop pointer movement, collection navigation, selectable garments, product details and a browser-local demonstration bag.

The supplied ready-to-run implementation is the most concrete reference for this pack. Use it verbatim when the user wants the existing Ruddo example, adapt its identity and collection when they have another brand, or use the room and interaction patterns as guidelines alongside their own references. Keep the user's existing project stack when integrating it. WordPress and WooCommerce are optional choices, not prerequisites.

## 1. Source, scope and delivery

The reference began with a short supplied showroom recording, followed by the explicit correction that the racks belong on separate walls and the camera should look around with mouse movement. Preserve those decisions. Do not place two parallel rails side by side along one flat back wall. The included source independently recreates the design using procedural geometry; the original garment models and original website source were not supplied. Do not claim the procedural garments are scans, production clothing assets or exact recovered originals.

The bundled version has no build step: `index.html`, `style.css`, `app.js`, `garments.js`, a locally bundled Three.js ES module, Outfit font and their required license notices. Extract the archive and serve its directory over HTTP, for example `python -m http.server 5188`, then open `http://localhost:5188`. Preserve the relative module and font paths. For another framework, move this scene and UI into the existing application without adding an unnecessary second framework.

The reference live example is [the Clothes Rack showroom](https://ruddo-clay-showroom.neuronsarealsocool.chatgpt.site/). The preview is a still of the corrected showroom, not a new product photograph or a separately generated video. The original supplied reference recording is not redistributed in this pack.

## 2. Visitor journey and composition

Begin outside the room, with the clothing rails intentionally soft behind the title. Present a sparse fixed header: the small overlapping double-disc mark at upper left, and `menu` plus `// cart` at upper right. The introduction centers `Clay-dyed / Workwear`, a very large, translucent `ruddo` wordmark with a registered mark, an offset orange label reading `Kiln-dyed`, `Slow-cut`, `SS27`, and a separate loose stack reading `Mended`, `Small runs`, `Monthly`.

The title should feel like typography placed in a physical space, with warm cloth, shadows and distance visible behind it. Use a restrained brown-to-sand room, off-white type and a sharp orange accent. Do not turn the opening into a conventional product-card grid. Keep the direct `ruddo.store` entry and the `scroll to walk in` cue near the lower center. The double-disc home control and the wordmark are different scales of the same simple identity.

Scrolling moves the camera forward. After entry, dissolve the introduction and sharpen the room. Show the back control, a subdued collection title when appropriate, an exploration hint and the fixed bottom Store/Men/Women navigation. Store frames both walls; Men and Women move toward the corresponding rack, turning the camera with the wall. Pointer movement adds a measured yaw/pitch response rather than moving all the content as one flat parallax layer.

## 3. Color, typography and layout values

Use Outfit, locally hosted from the included font, with Arial/sans-serif fallback and `font-display: swap`. The source palette is orange `#ff5c24`, ink `#241d16`, paper `#e7dfd1`, warm off-white `#fffdf4` and a dark room base around `#21170f`. Keep the supplied font's OFL notice.

The desktop header sits roughly 27px from the top and 32px from the sides. Its double disc is about 46×26px and the header links are approximately 16px. The desktop intro composition has a 560px-wide reference frame, its top around 30.5% of the screen, scaled by `min(1, viewportWidth / 1920)`. The reference display heading is 52px with close tracking; the oversized wordmark settles near 185px with strong negative tracking and a slight negative top margin. The orange label stack and manifesto should remain deliberately offset rather than mechanically centered underneath each other.

Keep the title translucent enough to see the room through it, while the main descriptive heading stays readable. The orange labels use dark text with tightly fitted rectangular fills. Panel surfaces are warm paper, with ink text, fine separators and clear controls. Match the supplied source for exact reuse; adjust typography and spacing coherently when adapting a longer brand name instead of retaining inappropriate fixed widths.

## 4. Three-dimensional room and lighting

Use a `PerspectiveCamera` with a 49° field of view, near plane 0.1 and far plane 180 as the reference baseline. The renderer uses antialiasing and alpha, an sRGB output color space, ACES filmic tone mapping, exposure around 1.16 and a device-pixel-ratio cap of 1.7. Share geometry and textures where possible so the showroom remains responsive.

The floor is a broad plane around 160×160 scene units, rotated horizontally just below y=0. Give it a warm sand shader that changes with distance from the two walls. Build two large wall planes meeting behind the racks, with rotations of +45° and −45°. In the supplied coordinate layout, wall centers are at x=−20/+20, y=23, z=11; each plane spans about `sqrt(2)×40` by 60 units. Shade one wall slightly darker, around 0.97 of the other, so the corner reads clearly. The wall shader transitions from light sand at floor level through brown into a nearly black ceiling region.

The men’s rail group is positioned near (−6.7, 0, −1.5) with a +π/4 rotation; the women’s group is near (6.7, 0, −1.5) with a −π/4 rotation. Store all garment, hit-target and contact-shadow positions relative to their own rotated rail group. Provide one helper that converts a rail-local point into a room/world point, and use it consistently for camera positions, look targets and projected product labels. Mixing local coordinates with unrotated world coordinates will break collection framing and hit testing.

Start with a warm hemisphere light (sky `#ece4d3`, ground `#55412b`, intensity about 2.4), a key directional light from (−8,12,8) around intensity 3.3, a fill from (10,8,5) around 1.8, and a rim from (2,7,−5) around 1.4. Use soft ambient contact shadows under the garments and each rail foot. The source draws a small radial canvas texture for these shadows; they should ground the objects without hard black ovals.

## 5. Clothing rails and procedural garments

Each rail is approximately 11.6 units wide and 5.96 units high. Model a thin, lightly imperfect metal tube with rounded upper corners and two tapered weighted feet. The source uses a curved tube radius near 0.031, warm metallic material `#bcb5a7`, and rough concrete-colored bases. Hang garments with visible wooden shoulders and small curved metal hooks; do not float clothing directly beneath an invisible rail.

Include 22 demonstration pieces, eleven in each collection. The color sequence is Coal `#242724`, Chalk `#e5e3d8`, Umber `#5e4d3a`, Ecru `#d0d0b8`, Indigo `#536c8b`, Mist `#a7bab9`, Terracotta `#b9583b`, Rose clay `#b88482`, Ochre `#b59b41`, Sage `#8d9d7d` and Ink `#222b2c`.

The men’s type sequence is shirt, hoodie, shirt, tee, pants, knit, tee, hoodie, shirt, knit, pants. The women’s sequence is shirt, hoodie, pants, tee, knit, pants, hoodie, tee, knit, shirt, shirt. Place them at rail-local x positions `−4.95 + index×0.99`, y near 5.19 and z near 0.02, scaled around 1.4. Give resting pieces an edge-on angle near 1.33 radians, with a small index-based variation. This lets hover turn a piece toward the visitor and makes the rail feel densely stocked.

Use garment silhouettes with sleeves, shoulders, neck openings, hems and separated trouser legs. The supplied geometry starts with 2D outlines, subdivides the triangles, displaces front and back panels into soft cloth folds, joins their edges and computes normals. Cotton should look matte: roughness around 0.94, zero metalness, double-sided panels and a subtle, repeating procedural fabric normal. Preserve the slightly uneven seam and fold structure rather than substituting glossy capsules or rigid boxes.

Differentiate garments with shirt plackets, small buttons, folded collars and pockets; hoodie hoods, drawstrings and kangaroo-pocket seams; knit ribs; sleeve cuffs; and trouser fly, belt loops, pockets and hems. Use the included `garments.js` as the authoritative implementation when exact reuse is requested. If the user supplies licensed production garment models, those may replace the approximations while retaining the interaction model. Model changes need visual review before publication.

## 6. Entry, camera states and mouse response

Normalize scroll progression as `clamp(scrollY / (viewportHeight×1.2), 0, 1)` and pass it through `t²(3−2t)`. The document runway is about 260vh. The reference enters Store when normalized scroll exceeds 0.42 and returns to the introduction below 0.08, provided a dialog is not open and a short programmatic-navigation suppression window has expired. Direct entry scrolls to roughly 1.2 viewport heights. Avoid smooth-scroll feedback that immediately returns a just-entered showroom to its initial state.

Initial camera reference: x=0, y≈3.9−0.4p, z≈22−4p on desktop, looking toward y≈5.3−2.4p. Narrow screens begin farther back, near z=31−3p. Store frames both rails from around (0,3.65,17.5), or z=29 on narrow screens, looking toward (0,2.9,−2).

A collection camera is computed in that rail’s local coordinates: y≈3.35, z≈9.8 on desktop or 10.7 on narrow screens, looking toward y=3.0. On phones, the x position tracks the selected piece. Selecting a product moves closer, near z=7 on desktop or 8 on narrow screens, and offsets desktop framing to leave room for the product panel.

Use time-based exponential easing with a factor near `1−exp(−dt×4.2)` and cap unusually long dt values around 0.05 seconds. Interpolate the camera position and look target separately. Normalize pointer position to −1…1, ease it, rotate the view direction around the world up axis and add a small vertical look offset. Approximate yaw limits are 0.14 radians in the intro, 0.38 in Store and 0.14 for a collection; vertical influence is smaller. Let Store have the widest look range.

Disable mouse-look for touch input, reduced motion, selected products and open dialogs. Clear or neutralize the pointer when it leaves the canvas, the window loses focus or collection navigation changes the view. UI controls must remain stable under the pointer. Scrolling should move the camera through the scene; pointer movement should look around within it.

## 7. Hover, selection and product labels

Use raycasting against simple, invisible pick volumes associated with the actual garment groups. A baseline pick box is around 0.78×3.4×0.95 units, offset below its hanger. Limit collection hit testing to that collection, and suppress it while a product or another dialog is open. The canvas cursor may indicate a selectable garment; essential navigation must also be available by keyboard and touch.

On hover or selection, ease the chosen garment toward a nearly frontal local rotation, around −0.025 radians, and draw it forward to local z≈1.25. Other pieces settle toward their own resting angles. An extremely small idle sway, about 0.008 radians, gives the rail life without turning it into a waving animation. Reduced motion removes this sway.

Project the active garment’s position to a small orange name label near its lower edge. Clamp the label into useful screen bounds and hide it when its projected position falls outside the safe area. Recalculate against the actual rotated wall, camera and viewport; a hard-coded label position will drift. Clicking a piece opens its details and focuses that garment.

## 8. Product panel and demonstration bag

Use an accessible native dialog sliding visually from the right, with warm paper fill and a subtly blurred backdrop. Desktop product panels are around 450px wide and full viewport height, with a close control, collection/season eyebrow, product name, price, a short description, color, XS/S/M/L/XL size choices, Add to bag, feedback and a fabric/care disclosure. Default to M and expose the selected size with `aria-pressed` as well as visual styling.

Demonstration prices in the source are tee $65, shirt $125, knit $135, hoodie $145 and trousers $155. Keep them clearly illustrative until an owner supplies genuine catalog data. Adding the same product and size increments quantity. A bag item is keyed by product ID and size; another size is a separate item. Bag rendering shows a color chip, item name, size, quantity, line total, an accessible Remove action, subtotal and Continue exploring.

Store bag state in local storage, validating recovered product IDs, sizes and positive integer quantities before using it. The included reference uses the compatibility key `ruddo-bag`. Handle malformed or unavailable browser storage without breaking the scene. Build item text using safe DOM text APIs rather than inserting untrusted catalog values as HTML.

This is a frontend showroom demo. Keep the visible statements that checkout is not connected and no payment is taken. Do not show an order-success state or pretend a bag operation is a completed purchase. If production commerce is requested, connect the user’s chosen real catalog, inventory, tax/shipping, checkout and order backend as separate work; WordPress/WooCommerce is one optional choice.

## 9. Navigation, dialogs and smaller screens

Store/Men/Women controls remain fixed along the bottom, with the active item orange and the others near-black. The desktop baseline is about 610×34px; the narrow layout is the viewport width minus 40px, 38px high and around 18px from the bottom. Collection selection updates camera orientation, active state, accessible pressed state and the faint collection heading. Back returns a collection to Store and Store to the introduction. Home resets the intro immediately without leaving a partially scrolled title.

The menu dialog contains The store, Men and Women navigation and a short brand note. Selecting a destination closes the menu, moves the camera and restores usable page controls. Synchronize `aria-expanded` with the menu’s actual open state. Native Escape behavior, visible close controls, sensible focus return and body scroll handling are required for every dialog. Avoid keyboard traps outside a correctly open modal.

At widths below about 700px, recompose the header and intro, move the camera back and show Previous garment, Explore a piece and Next garment controls for collection views. The intro reference is roughly 340px wide, with a 29px heading, 118px wordmark and smaller staggered label stacks. Ensure that any longer adapted brand fits instead of overflowing this reference frame. Product and bag panels must stay within screen bounds and retain internal scrolling for their content.

Touch users can move along the chosen rack with the arrow controls or a horizontal swipe exceeding roughly 40px. Keep vertical scrolling available for entering and leaving the room. Wrap the selected index within the collection. Keyboard users must be able to reach collection navigation and explicit product exploration without a mouse; the supplied desktop exploration controls become visible on focus. Never make hover the only path to product information.

## 10. Motion, failure and performance

Respect reduced motion for the camera, garment sway, blur and transitions. Keep the scene’s final readable states, controls and actual product information available. Avoid autoplay sound. The included source has a useful reduced-motion baseline; production refinements should also react to a changed preference during a session and avoid wasting rendering work while hidden or idle.

If WebGL cannot initialize, show an honest fallback with a reachable way to browse product details. A production adaptation should make the full collection reachable in that fallback, rather than only a single demonstration item. Do not remove the normal document and leave a blank canvas. Loading, module/font failure and missing assets should have understandable outcomes.

Cap rendering resolution, reuse geometry/materials, avoid rebuilding clothing on every frame and dispose of GPU resources if this scene mounts/unmounts inside an application. Test high-DPI phones and short viewports as well as wide monitors. The runnable source is an independently authored example with procedural approximations and a demonstration bag, not a connected production shop.

The source archive also contains the original component license files. These URLs are part of the complete prompt and should remain in copied and downloaded versions. Public access does not grant additional rights to another brand’s identity, reference material or third-party assets.

## 12. Acceptance and adaptation

Verify the opening composition and its responsive title scale; visible separation of the two perpendicular walls; scroll-in and reverse-scroll behavior; direct Store entry without a bounce back to the intro; collection camera turns; mouse yaw/pitch; hover orientation and projected labels; keyboard/touch exploration; size selection; duplicate-item quantity; separate sizes; remove/subtotal; local-storage recovery; menu, home, back and Escape; reduced motion; WebGL failure; and both desktop and narrow layouts.

Do not put an entire uncropped sheet inside a cover or a poster.

Preload all four sheets with `Image` objects. Wait for successful load/decode before replacing the loading state with the completed shelf. A failed sheet must produce a legible, named fallback face and an actionable retry message; it must not leave an endless loader or a completely blank archive. ## Typography and tokens

Self-host the fonts and retain their licenses. A single-file delivery can embed the font bytes as base64 WOFF2 in `@font-face` rules. Keep fonts outside CSS sprite coordinates: the asset art already contains its own display lettering.

| Noto Sans JP Big | 800, subset containing `映画の記憶` | Large decorative kanji; use `font-display:block` for this subset |
| Noto Serif SC | 700 | Optional compatibility embedding; it has no visible role in this composition |

The sans stack is `"Inter Tight","Noto Sans JP",system-ui,sans-serif`. The serif stack is `"Newsreader",Georgia,serif`. Ensure Japanese glyphs render correctly, including the large decorative characters; do not ship missing-glyph boxes while claiming font fidelity.

--sheet:#F3F0EA;
--ink:#141414;
--muted:#6D6A63;

--ease:cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1);

The main document has a paper background, hidden viewport overflow and antialiased text. Avoid accidental text selection during a shelf drag; keep reading text and useful metadata selectable in the detail view. Hide the ordinary pointer only on fine-pointer devices when the working custom cursor is present. Preserve it for coarse pointers, failed initialization and accessibility fallbacks.

Use a shared `.lbl` style: Inter Tight 600, 10.5px, line-height 1, letter-spacing .14em, uppercase. A small boxed label is an inline flex box, 21px high, with 8px horizontal padding and a 1px dark rule.

Cover the composition with a fixed, pointer-transparent grain layer at z-index 40, multiply blend and opacity .6. Use a repeating 220px SVG tile with `feTurbulence` type `fractalNoise`, base frequency .85, three octaves and stitched tiles. Its color matrix rows are `0 0 0 0 .45`, `0 0 0 0 .42`, `0 0 0 0 .38`, `0 0 0 .22 0`. The grain is decorative and must not intercept input or enter the accessibility tree.

## Desktop placement

Use fixed viewport placement for the archive stage. Measure the actual resolved `--H` through a probe element with `height:var(--H)` so CSS and JavaScript remain in agreement after resizing. Convert `--cy` to the corresponding viewport Y coordinate before calculating transforms.

### Header and large lettering

The top bar is 76px high with 36px side padding, cobalt text and space between its two groups. On the left, arrange a home control labelled `THE FILM ROOM`, a 40 × 1px line and `FILM ARCHIVE`, with 16px gaps. On the right, arrange `FILMS`, `ABOUT`, `JOURNAL` with 34px gaps and a 26 × 12px menu button built from two 1.5px lines.

Make these controls meaningful. Films returns to the shelf or closes an auxiliary panel. About opens concise archive information. Journal opens an actual local reading panel or entry list. The menu exposes the same destinations on smaller screens. Do not ship `href="#"` links that silently do nothing. Use the neutral interface identity consistently, including inside the detail sheet.

The kanji columns sit behind the tapes at z-index 1, use `writing-mode:vertical-rl`, the large subset font at weight 800, size `min(19vh,12.5vw)`, line-height 1.02 and letter-spacing .02em. Put `映画` at left 2.4vw/top 13vh and `の記憶` at right 2.4vw/top 9vh. Clip the following layered background into transparent text: a repeating 3 × 3px radial dot, `rgba(64,82,138,.55)` from 0–36% and transparent from 40%, over a flat `rgba(110,122,160,.26)` wash. Mark both columns as decorative.

### Shelf, faces and grounding

Centre the floor shadow at Y `cy+.47H`. Its width is `min(96vw,3.6H)` and its height is `.26H`. Use `radial-gradient(50% 50% at 50% 40%, rgba(40,32,20,.30), rgba(40,32,20,.10) 55%, transparent 72%)`.

The full-width shelf starts at `cy-H/2-50px`, has height `H+100px`, perspective 1400px with origin 50% 50%, z-index 10 and `touch-action:pan-y`. A zero-sized, centred stage and every zero-sized tape node use `transform-style:preserve-3d`.

Each tape has two faces of height H with their top at `-H/2`. Centre their widths around the tape's local origin. Use 2px radii and hidden back faces. The narrow spine has width `ws` and transform `translateZ(d/2)`. The broad front has width `d` and transform `rotateY(90deg) translateZ(ws/2)`. The front's shadow is `0 34px 60px -30px rgba(20,16,10,.6)`. Add a black `::after` shading layer to each face, controlled by its own `--shade` value. Decorative faces must not add duplicate keyboard stops.

Put a 42px circular open affordance near the active cover's lower-left corner: X `W/2-d/2-6`, Y `cy+.36H`. Give it a 1px cobalt border, `rgba(236,232,224,.8)` fill and a 12px cobalt triangle. It opens the film's detail sheet, not an imaginary video player. Its accessible name must communicate that action.

### Caption, arrows, ruler and footer

Centre a caption grid at Y `cy+H/2+4.2vh`, with a 10px gap. Its line masks have a responsive width capped at 640px and constrained to 80vw. The title is cobalt Inter Tight 600, `clamp(28px,3.4vw,46px)`, tracking -.015em. Below it, show `ROMAJI / Japanese title` in cobalt at 9.5px, weight 600 and .24em tracking. Follow it with a centred 18 × 1px cobalt rule, then the ink year/genre line at 10.5px, weight 500 and .08em tracking. Use `YEAR — GENRE` and uppercase the genre visually.

Place two 44px arrow buttons on the title's line at centre X plus or minus `min(19vw,250px)`. Their 24 × 12px SVGs have a 1.2px cobalt stroke; the left path is `M6 1L1 6l5 5M1 6h23`, and the right is its mirror. Give them explicit previous/next labels, visible keyboard focus and adequate touch targets.

The ruler has 36px side gutters, bottom offset 64px and height 40px. Draw its 1px cobalt line 12px from the top at .75 opacity. Include every year from 1955 through 1990. Ticks at multiples of five are 13px tall at .75 opacity; other ticks are 7px at .4. Major labels use Inter Tight 500, 9.5px, cobalt, below the rule. Left-align 1955 and right-align 1990. The selection dot is 9px and cobalt. The whole intended ruler hit area should respond to selecting a year without requiring a click on a 1px line.

Place a small cobalt footer 36px from both sides and 24px above the bottom. Use a truthful demo/collection line such as `THE FILM ROOM / FICTIONAL FILM COLLECTION`. Do not claim ownership of the artwork or offer dead social links. If social controls are included, connect them to actual destinations or use clearly labelled local information actions.

## The collection

Use the following shelf order and structured fields: ID, display title, romanised title, Japanese title, release year, genre, duration in minutes and synopsis. The works are fictional; these descriptions do not imply that full films are supplied. The initial selected record is index 5, Noon in Ashes.

Render three copies of the twelve records, creating 36 virtual tape nodes. A node's virtual index is `v=copy*12+i`. Start both the displayed shelf position `s` and target position `T` at `17`, which is `12+5`. Use data-driven rendering rather than separately maintained captions and faces.

## Exact arc geometry

Measure H after font/layout initialization and on relevant viewport changes. Let W be the viewport width, `cy` the shelf centre Y coordinate, and P the shelf perspective. The symbols below are independent of CSS pixel dimensions of the source sheets.

```text
ws = H * 142/840
d = H * 474/900
gap = H * .035
U = H * 1.3                  desktop
U = H * 1.05                 viewport width below 768px
P = 1400
```

The relative virtual index is wrapped into `[-18,18)`:

```text
r = mod(v-s+18,36)-18
mod(a,n) = ((a % n)+n) % n
B(r) = (r+sin(PI*r)/PI)/2    when abs(r)<1
B(r) = sign(r)*.5            otherwise
u = r*(ws+gap)+(d-ws+1.4*gap)*B(r)
sc = 1/(1+(abs(u)/U)^1.6)
```

The extra B term opens a smooth gap for the turning front rather than letting its neighbours collide. Compress screen-space X with an integral of the scale function. Precompute `XS` from zero to `3U` in 2px increments, accumulating `2/(1+(u/U)^1.6)`. Obtain `xsc(u)` by looking up/interpolating `XS[abs(u)/2]` and applying the sign of u. Recompute this table after H or U changes. Do not use a straight, uniformly spaced row as a substitute.

For every visible tape on every frame:

```text
smoothstep(a) = a*a*(3-2*a)   for a clamped to [0,1]
o = smoothstep(max(0,1-abs(r)))
hide node when abs(u)>U*1.95
k = 1/sc
z = P*(1-k)+o*H*.1
x = xsc(u)*k
y = (H*.5*(1-sc)*.42+o*H*.012-lift*H*.05)*k
rotateY = sign(u)*min(1,abs(u)/U)*26*(1-o)-90*o+tiltY*o
rotateX = tiltX*o
transform = translate3d(x,y,z) rotateX(rotateX deg) rotateY(rotateY deg)
z-index = round(3000+z)
spine shade = min(.6,o*.55+(1-sc)*.32)
front shade = (1-o)*.82
```

`o=1` gives the selected front and `o=0` gives a spine. For a hovered non-active tape, meaning `abs(r)>.5`, ease its lift towards 1 with `1-exp(-12*dt)`; otherwise ease it towards zero. Keep nodes outside the cutoff noninteractive and hidden from assistive technology. Avoid forced layout reads inside the per-tape loop.

## Motion and selection state

Use delta time in seconds and cap it at .05. The shelf uses exponential interpolation:

```text
s += (T-s)*(1-exp(-rate*dt))
rate = 5.2                   normal movement
rate = 18                    while dragging
```

Rebase s and T by matching whole twelve-film loops when the position drifts beyond four loops, preserving their difference and the displayed sequence. The active record is `mod(round(s),12)`. Change the caption only when this record changes; derive slide direction from `sign(T-s)` with a stable fallback for direct/snap selections.

Calculate the ruler year by interpolating between the records at `floor(s)` and `floor(s)+1`. Across the 1989-to-1958 seam, switch years at the half-step rather than sweeping the dot backwards across every intermediate year. Ease the displayed marker at `1-exp(-14*dt)`; jump immediately when the difference exceeds six years. Its horizontal fraction is `(year-1955)/35`.

Enable active-cover tilt only when the pointer is within `.55d` of viewport centre X and `.55H` of cy, the shelf is settled to `abs(T-s)<.3`, and no detail/panel is open. In that region, target `tiltY=(mx-W/2)/(.55d)*8` degrees and `tiltX=-(my-cy)/(H/2)*5` degrees. Elsewhere target `tiltY=(mx-W/2)/W*4` and `tiltX=0`. Ease both using `1-exp(-7*dt)`. Disable decorative pointer tilt for coarse pointers and reduced motion.

The lower-left open ring has scale `smoothstep(max(0,1-abs(T-s)*3))`; set its scale to zero while the detail sheet is open.

## Input behaviour

- Clicking a non-active tape selects its nearest equivalent position by setting `T=round(T+r)`. Clicking the settled active cover opens its detail. Suppress click activation after a drag.
- Previous and next arrow buttons step by one. Left and right keyboard arrows provide the same movement when the archive owns keyboard navigation. Enter opens the selected film. Escape closes the topmost open panel or detail.
- A pointer drag begins only after movement exceeds 5px. Retain the starting target `T0` and set `T=T0-dx/(ws+gap)`. Snap T to its nearest integer on release. Handle pointer cancellation and release capture cleanly. A vertical gesture must remain usable for scrolling a mobile detail.
- Wheel movement uses whichever of deltaX/deltaY has the larger absolute magnitude, adds `delta/(ws+gap)*.5` to T, and snaps after 160ms without a new wheel event. Normalize non-pixel wheel delta modes. Do not navigate the shelf or prevent detail scrolling while any detail or auxiliary panel is open.
- Clicking the ruler maps its X coordinate to a year, finds the nearest record year, and selects the shortest path around the twelve-record loop. Clamp pointer coordinates at the endpoints. Give keyboard users equivalent year/record selection through semantic controls.

Do not let global shortcuts intercept typing or activate underlying archive controls while a modal is open. Keep one authoritative collection selection so caption, poster, ruler, accessible name and highlighted state cannot disagree during quick navigation.

## Caption transition

Each caption line is a clipped mask. On a record change, append the new text span over the existing one and translate it from `dir*105%` vertically to zero. Move outgoing spans from their current computed transform to `-dir*105%`, then remove them. Use 650ms, `cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1)` and `fill:both`. During rapid stepping, cancel or supersede existing transitions without leaving orphaned spans or exposing all captions at once. Do not fade text. Announce the selected title/year through a restrained live region after selection settles, not on every animation frame.

## Full-screen detail sheet

Use a fixed sheet with `--sheet` background, z-index 60 and a true closed/hidden state. Desktop content is a two-column grid with a 4vw gap and padding `110px 6vw 56px 7vw`. Place a boxed `CLOSE / 閉じる` control at left 36px/top 28px. Put the cobalt archive identity at top right. Give the sheet dialog semantics and label it with the selected title.

Vertically centre the text column, cap it at 520px and use an 18px gap. Put every entrance-animated item inside a separate overflow mask, in this order:

1. Cobalt romanised/Japanese subtitle using `.lbl`.
2. Cobalt Inter Tight 600 title at `clamp(44px,5.2vw,80px)` and -.03em tracking.
3. Muted year, genre and runtime: `YEAR / GENRE / N min`.
4. Newsreader roman synopsis at 17px/1.5 and max-width 42ch.
5. Newsreader italic muted collection note, such as `A fictional release from The Film Room collection. 監督作品`.
6. A 44px cobalt-outline film-availability action.

No full films or trailers are included with these sheets. In this build label the final action `FILM NOT AVAILABLE / 本編未公開` or an equally clear unavailable state and provide readable explanatory text. Do not create a fake playable video, a dead watch link or an alert pretending that a film has been opened. A later authorized film URL may replace this state without changing the sheet layout.

The right column holds the poster SVG with `viewBox="0 0 474 900"` and a height capped at `min(100%,78vh)`. Apply the supplied front crop, not the spine. Use a rectangular clip for the poster bounds and a second mask for the ink reveal. Distort a group of seven white mask circles with an SVG filter: `feTurbulence` type `fractalNoise`, base frequency .011, three octaves, seed 7, feeding a displacement map with scale 120 and R/G displacement channels.

| Circle centre X | Centre Y | Additional delay in ms |
|---|---|---|
| 150 | 330 | 0 |
| 340 | 600 | 120 |
| 250 | 120 | 220 |
| 90 | 760 | 300 |
| 400 | 250 | 360 |
| 260 | 860 | 420 |
| 230 | 470 | 180 |

### Open sequence

Snap the selection target to its current intended record, fill all detail fields and point the SVG image at the correct cropped sheet. Reset all mask-circle radii to zero. Read the projected bounding rectangle of the actual front face with `getBoundingClientRect()` after its geometry has been updated. Derive viewport inset distances from that rectangle.

Show the detail sheet and animate its clip path from `inset(top right bottom left round 3px)` to `inset(0 round 0)` over 1050ms using `cubic-bezier(.76,0,.18,1)`. The initial paper rectangle must align with the selected cover; a generic centre-screen scale is not equivalent.

Animate the six text items upwards from `translateY(110%)` to zero over 900ms, with delays `620+i*75` ms. At 520ms plus each circle's additional delay, grow that circle's radius from zero to 720 over 1250ms using ease-out cubic, `1-(1-t)^3`. Update radii through the existing animation loop; do not start another permanent rAF loop.

Move focus into the dialog, keep Tab/Shift+Tab within it and make the underlying stage inert while it is open. Preserve a reference to the opener for focus restoration. Allow Escape and the close button to work during the entrance as well as after it.

### Close sequence

Read the current selected cover rectangle again, including after a viewport resize. Animate the sheet clip from full-screen back to that rectangle over 850ms with the same sheet easing. Then hide it, cancel outstanding text/clip animations, reset reveal state and restore the underlying stage. Restore focus to the opener or the selected cover's accessible control if the original opener is no longer present. Guard rapid open/close actions against stale completion callbacks.

## Fine-pointer cursor

Use the custom cursor only on a fine pointer after successful initialization. It is a fixed 58px element at z-index 100, pointer-transparent and hidden from the accessibility tree. Compose a 1.5px ink ring, a 6px ink dot, and a hidden white two-line `OPEN / 開く` label in Inter Tight 600 at 10px. Ease its displayed location towards the pointer at `1-exp(-16*dt)`.

Over the settled, openable cover, scale the ring to 1.75, fill it cobalt and reveal the label by scale/clip. Over an inactive spine, use scale .72. Over a button, link or the ruler, use scale .55 and hide the centre dot. Ring-transform timing is .5s; colour and dot changes .4s; label movement .45s. Reset correctly when the pointer leaves the viewport, opens a dialog or changes pointer type. Visible keyboard focus must remain independent of this decoration.

## Phone composition, 767px and below

Use `--H:min(68vw,40svh)` and `--cy:43%`, with the smaller depth-falloff U specified above. The composition is deliberately rearranged rather than merely scaled down.

- Make the top bar 60px high with 16px side gutters. Hide the desktop text navigation, retain a usable menu button and shorten the divider to 22px.
- Set the large kanji to 22vw and opacity .8. Keep it behind the artwork, not behind essential small labels.
- Use a 27px caption title. Place the arrow controls at the screen edges, 118px above the bottom, leaving the title centred and readable.
- Give the ruler 16px side gutters and a 54px bottom offset. Hide alternate major year labels to prevent collisions while preserving all tick marks and navigation.
- Reflow the detail into one scrolling column. Put the poster first at 46svh, followed by the text; use a 42px detail title. Keep the close action reachable, support normal vertical scrolling and accommodate safe-area insets without clipping content.
- Remove the custom cursor and decorative pointer tilt. Horizontal finger movement scrubs the shelf; a tap opens the selected cover. Preserve the drag threshold so a swipe does not open a film accidentally.

Recalculate geometry on viewport changes. Check short landscape viewports, mobile browser chrome changes and narrow widths as well as a tall phone. Essential navigation, caption and ruler must not overlap. When viewport height is insufficient, choose a smaller responsive shelf or allow an accessible overflow treatment rather than hiding controls outside the screen.

## Reduced motion and accessibility

Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` on load and if it changes. Set the shelf position directly to its target, make hover lift immediate, remove decorative tilt and cursor lag, replace caption slides with immediate swaps, and use 1ms sheet/text transitions. Treat the ink animation as already five seconds old so the complete poster is immediately visible. Keep the alternate presentation fully functional, not an inert poster.

Use semantic buttons and navigation, readable accessible names and clear focus indicators. Keep the 36 visual copies from producing 36 confusing duplicate controls: offer a single understandable twelve-record selection model or a selected-cover control plus previous/next actions and a correctly labelled film list. Do not hide essential film names only in CSS background art. Decorative masks, grain and kanji should be inaccessible. Make small visible labels sit inside practical 44px interaction targets where relevant. Honor system contrast preferences where feasible without losing readable content.

The detail and auxiliary panels need focus containment, Escape, background inertness and focus restoration. Any font or image loading error must leave metadata and navigation operable. Do not trap the keyboard in the shelf, prevent browser zoom, or block native vertical scrolling inside a phone detail. Use a no-script message with useful collection context if the shelf depends on JavaScript.

## Completion checks

Verify the delivered interface with the actual hosted sheets and inspect the crops visually. Check that the opening record is Noon in Ashes, every front matches its spine/title, the three replacement spines are used, and all twelve records appear in the correct order. Test both loop directions, long drags, wheel bursts, quick repeated arrow presses, endpoint ruler clicks and selection after resizing.

Confirm that far spines shrink, darken, sink and pack together; the selected front opens adequate space between its neighbours; and no face appears reversed or as a full sprite sheet. Inspect the start, middle and end of the clip expansion and ink reveal. Open/close during an animation, resize with the detail open and verify that the closing paper returns to the current cover.

Check desktop and phone viewport compositions, keyboard-only operation, visible focus, focus restoration, real panel destinations, mobile detail scrolling, pointer cancellation, reduced motion and simulated image-loading failure. A desktop phone-sized viewport is a responsive check, not evidence of testing a physical device. Run appropriate syntax/build checks for the chosen stack and report verification limits honestly.

Deliver the full implementation and a working public example when publication is requested. Keep the full working prompt, all four asset URLs and any required notices together in the pack. Do not replace an independently existing adapted example when publishing this faithful VHS version; update this pack's example link to the new correct build.

## Reuse and media workflow

Use this independently authored working prompt verbatim, adapt it, or combine its locked elements with other references. Keep the current frontend unless a platform change is requested. Replicate is the default for any new media generation; verify the chosen model, scope, current cost and retry allowance before spending. The four supplied sheets can be reused under their existing unchanged-media approval. Show any newly selected, newly generated or materially altered media in chat and obtain approval before placing it on a public site, asset host or release. Preserve required font and third-party license notices.


## Example implementation refinements

The public VHS example also exposes a Reduce motion switch in its navigation menu; it combines that preference with the operating system setting. Below 500px height, landscape composition reduces tape height and moves the caption above the ruler. For desktop-width landscape, use H=32svh, cy=35%, a 56px top bar, 26px caption title, 4px caption gaps, and the ruler 44px above the bottom. Phone-width landscape uses H=38svh, cy=40%, a 22px title and a 38px ruler bottom offset. Keep the cursor native on phone-width layouts. The example uses the fictional collection label rather than claiming authorship of supplied artwork.

## Live website reference

[View live VHS archive](https://curved-film-archive.neuronsarealsocool.chatgpt.site)

Dedicated twelve-film VHS implementation with The Film Room interface branding, approved sprite sheets and the original curved shelf and ink reveal.

Build a single-screen cinematic landing page for Auralis, a fictional harbour-front penthouse firm. The visitor starts outside a pair of black lacquer doors. When they part, the view looks straight down on an illuminated rooftop pool. A fast camera tilt opens the harbour out to the horizon. The film dissolves into a live composition where the skyline crosses the foot of “Harbour” and a man rises into the foreground. At rest, the weather continues moving behind the buildings.

## Hosted media

Load the five 2000px WebP stills in one shared frame. Preserve the transparency of the skyline and balcony cutouts. Stream both videos directly from the linked MP4 files and preload the linked variable font.

| Role | Resource |

| doors | https://lapis-slate-xvar.here.now/library/rainy-harbour-penthouse/media/doors.webp |
| aerial | https://lapis-slate-xvar.here.now/library/rainy-harbour-penthouse/media/aerial.webp |
| back | https://lapis-slate-xvar.here.now/library/rainy-harbour-penthouse/media/back.webp |
| mid | https://lapis-slate-xvar.here.now/library/rainy-harbour-penthouse/media/mid.webp |
| front | https://lapis-slate-xvar.here.now/library/rainy-harbour-penthouse/media/front.webp |
| tilt | https://lapis-slate-xvar.here.now/library/rainy-harbour-penthouse/media/tilt.mp4 |
| rain | https://lapis-slate-xvar.here.now/library/rainy-harbour-penthouse/media/rain.mp4 |
| font | https://lapis-slate-xvar.here.now/library/rainy-harbour-penthouse/media/font.woff2 |

Keep the [Inter font license](https://lapis-slate-xvar.here.now/library/rainy-harbour-penthouse/inter-OFL.txt) with redistributed copies of the font.

## Compose the final frame first

Use Inter throughout, with the supplied variable Latin font preloaded and displayed with swap. Set the tab title to “Auralis — Above the Harbour” and the description to “Auralis: harbour-view penthouses above a city that never sleeps. Above the harbour.”

Fill the viewport with an isolated, clipped hero on #0D0A22. Use a 100svh composition with a 520px minimum in ordinary orientations. Fit short landscape screens to their available height. Centre a 16:9 stage sized to cover the viewport. At 1440 × 900 the stage is 1600 × 900 and extends 80px past either side.

1. Storm sky and harbour water, two interchangeable rain videos, then a top shade from rgba(13,8,40,.45) to transparent across the upper 45%. Pivot the back plane at 50% 40%.

# Bird species atlas

Build an interactive field-guide hero for two birds: Hoopoe and Kingfisher, with Kingfisher selected initially. The page combines a left editorial sidebar, two specimen tabs above a large central stage, and an independently scrolling facts panel on the right. One transparent WebGL canvas spans the entire hero so an enlarged specimen can overlap the interface without panel clipping. There is no video. Use the existing project stack; a single HTML page with inline CSS/module JavaScript is the buildless reference treatment. WordPress is optional. New media uses Replicate by default and requires agreed spending and in-chat approval before publication.

## Assets, libraries and type

Use the approved two PNG illustrations and two GLB specimens in the hosted asset map. Keep each image/model pair associated with its species; the PNG is the loading/failure fallback and also supplies the tab thumbnail and close-up lens. Load the active specimen first and preload the other later. The reference library is Three.js with GLTFLoader, DRACOLoader, MeshoptDecoder and RoomEnvironment. Pin a compatible verified release and decoder path rather than mixing addon versions. Implement pointer interaction directly, without OrbitControls.

Display type is Newsreader400/500 with italic400, body Nunito Sans400/600/700. Use serif fallbacks Iowan Old Style/Georgia and sans Segoe UI/system-ui. Render line icons as inline24×24 SVG symbols, stroke1.5, round caps/joins, usually20px, rather than emoji or an icon font.

Day tokens: background#f6f1e7, panel#fbf8f1, line#e7e0d1, ink#1b1a17, muted#6d685d, sage#4d5a3d, sage text white, sage tint#e9ebdc, chip#efeadd, shadowRGB60,48,28. Dusk: background#14170f, panel#1b1f15, line#2d3324, ink#f2ecdf, muted#a8a392, sage#a9b98a, sage text#14170f, tint#283020, chip#262b1d, shadow black. Ease cubic-bezier(.22,.8,.24,1); palette changes .6seconds. Focus rings are2px sage with2px offset.

## Desktop layout

Above1100px, fill100dvh with grid columns196px / minmax(0,1fr) / clamp(300px,27vw,356px). The absolute full-hero canvas has z-index5 and pointer-events:none; interaction belongs to the accessible stage element. Hide page overflow only when every control and fact remains reachable internally.

Sidebar padding22px12px18px24px, right border1px. Set the atlas name in26px Newsreader, then navigation for Home, Featured, Songbirds, Kingfishers, Owls, Hummingbirds, Raptors and Waders. Example group counts are34,8,11,15,12,9; do not imply those additional species are interactive until implemented. Selected Featured uses sage tint. The stage fills available space, has tabindex0, a grab cursor and touch-action:none limited to this specimen interaction area. A ground shadow sits at bottom15%, width min(62%,460px), height44px and .22 opacity, shrinking/fading during switches. Add a30px preparing ring and clear loading text; failed GLB uses the species PNG. A top-right drag/zoom hint disappears permanently after first interaction. The left icon rail has four38px circular controls with9px gaps: zoom in, zoom out, expand and light. Use aria-label/aria-pressed and distinguish active states. The bottom46px turn pill contains quarter-turn left,360° and quarter-turn right; put a centred italic caption below.

## Species data

Hoopoe: Upupa epops, family UPUPIDAE. Tags Ground forager/Crested/Migrant. Describe cinnamon, black and white plumage, a long curved probing bill, a crest raised into a fan and loose butterfly-like flight. Traits: length25–29cm; wingspan44–48cm; insects/larvae/grubs; Europe/Asia/Africa. Habitat orchards, vineyards and dry grassland. Caption “A crown raised, and the orchard takes notice.” The close-up explains black feather tips in the raised crest; lens position62%22%. Featured title “A crown of cinnamon.” with short text about broad barred wings and its recognizable call.

Kingfisher: Alcedo atthis, family ALCEDINIDAE. Tags River bird/Diver/Iridescent. Describe a small brightly coloured river/lake bird known for hunting dives. Traits: length16–17cm; dive speed up to40km/h as supplied example data; small fish/insects; Europe/Asia. Habitat slow rivers, streams and lakes. Caption “Blink, and the river keeps its secret.” Close-up discusses the mosaic of plumage structure/colour; lens position24%30%. Use alpha/antialias renderer, DPR≤2, sRGB output, NeutralToneMapping, exposure1.05.
